headline: Chips Lead a Brutal Friday Selloff as Markets Brace for a Geopolitical Week
body_html:
Wall Street ended the week on its back foot. In Friday's session, October 30, 344 of the 530 stocks we track fell and only 182 rose. Semiconductors took the worst of it, dropping 6.04%, while software slid 1.14% and industrials and materials gave up 1.56% and 1.75%. Healthcare lost 1.29%.

The pain was concentrated in growth names. Roblox fell 18.05%, Bright Horizons 17.92%, Twilio 15.24%, Sandisk 13.47%, Datadog 11.5% and Coherent 11.34%. Pockets of strength were mostly in housing and consumer names. Homebuilders rose 1.75% and energy added 0.43%. Capri jumped 16.31%, Cavco gained 13.11%, GoDaddy 10.72% and Mohawk 7.25%.

Traders return Monday, November 2, with the Middle East high on the agenda. Reports of tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and a US order for non-emergency staff to leave Saudi Arabia keep the energy market on alert. A St. Louis Fed official's call for tighter policy "soon" adds a rate question, and mediation efforts over Iran and Ukraine are worth watching.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Tanker Incidents Keep Oil Traders Wary
briefs.body: Iranian naval officials said four tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, and security sources pointed to limpet mines on one vessel. Separately, the UAE said a tanker leak was stopped and pollution was easing. Energy was the only major sector besides homebuilders to finish Friday higher, up 0.43%.

briefs.headline: Washington Pulls Non-Emergency Staff From Saudi Arabia
briefs.body: The US ordered non-emergency personnel to leave Saudi Arabia over security risks. A Saudi-led coalition also said it downed a drone over the oil-rich Eastern Region. Together the reports sharpen the regional risk premium heading into Monday's open.

briefs.headline: Fed's Musalem Says Tighter Policy Is Needed Soon
briefs.body: St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem argued that monetary policy needs to tighten before long. A hawkish tilt matters for growth stocks, which absorbed heavy selling on Friday. Investors will look for more central-bank commentary to judge whether the rate debate is shifting.

briefs.headline: Pakistan Sees Room for Iran-US Mediation
briefs.body: Pakistan's military is said to be cautiously optimistic about mediating between Iran and the United States. Any diplomatic progress could ease the tensions around Gulf shipping lanes. For now, the optimism is tentative, and the week's tanker headlines cut the other way.

briefs.headline: Bitcoin Holds Up Better After Record Exchange Hack
briefs.body: Bitcoin proved more resilient than many expected after what was described as a record hack at the Binance exchange. The steadier tone contrasted with Friday's sharp drop in chips and software, though traders will watch whether it lasts into the new week.

briefs.headline: Pricier Cocoa Puts Candymakers Under Pressure
briefs.body: Rising chocolate costs made Halloween more expensive this year, and Hershey may feel the squeeze. Consumer stocks fell 0.46% on Friday as a group, yet some names, such as Capri, posted large gains. Input costs remain a theme for food and treat makers.
